_meta.what: The post shapes the writer can use. A shape is a structure: it says what beats a post has and in what order. It never says what the post is about. The subject, facts and voice come from the brand through the contract.
_meta.files: Each shape is described in full in <id>.md in this folder, with a worked example for a fictional bakery.

fields.id: Stable identifier. Other parts of the Factory look shapes up by id, and it is stored on each post. Never rename one.
fields.name: What to call it when talking to a person.
fields.best_for: Platforms where the shape works best, strongest first. Keys match profiles.json, so 'twitter' means X.
fields.length: short (up to about 600 characters), medium (about 600 to 1,000), long (about 1,000 to 2,500). The figures describe the fullest version, on the first platform in best_for. On X anything above 280 characters becomes a thread.
fields.identity: Who may use it: 'any', 'person' (an identity that says I) or 'company' (an identity that says we and you).
fields.when: One line on when to choose it.

_meta.rule: Fill a shape only from the contract you were given. Never invent a fact, number, quote or customer. If the contract cannot fill a beat, drop the beat or choose another shape.

shapes.name: Three Tips
shapes.when: The reader wants to do something and you can give them three things to do this week, each with a reason and a concrete detail.

shapes.name: Myth vs Reality
shapes.when: One common belief is wrong or half right, and you have a fact or example that settles it quickly.

shapes.name: Problem, Cost, Way Out
shapes.when: The reader already feels a specific problem, and you can give them a real first step out of it.

shapes.name: Three Objections, Answered
shapes.when: People want the thing and still do not act, and you know from real conversations the reasons they give.

shapes.name: Five Lessons
shapes.when: There is a real stretch of experience to draw on (years, projects, customers) and each lesson has a moment behind it.

shapes.name: Bullet Insight
shapes.when: You have one sharp observation and a handful of short, parallel examples that prove it.

shapes.name: Five Questions
shapes.when: You want real conversation, and the audience has experiences worth hearing about.

shapes.name: Before and After Story
shapes.when: A real person went through a real change, and the contract holds the before, the after and the time between them.
